overview:
This ten-day private journey crosses Morocco from the red city of Marrakech to the spiritual capital of Fes, by way of the High Atlas, the kasbahs and oases of the south and the dunes of the Sahara. It is built to be unhurried. You have two full days in Marrakech, a night at Ait Ben Haddou so you see the ksar at sunset, a whole day around Ouarzazate, a night in the Erg Chebbi dunes, and the return north split in two with a night in Midelt, so that no driving day is exhausting. Two guided days, one in each imperial city, frame the trip.

After a first evening at Jemaa el-Fna and a guided day of palaces, souks and gardens in Marrakech, you cross the Tizi n'Tichka pass to Ait Ben Haddou. The next day is spent around Ouarzazate – the Taourirt Kasbah, the film studios and the hidden palm oasis of Fint. Then you head east along the Road of a Thousand Kasbahs and through the Todra gorge to Merzouga, where a camel trek takes you to a desert camp. After sunrise over the dunes you return west to the Dades valley, then turn north through the Ziz gorges and over the eastern High Atlas to Midelt, below the Jebel Ayachi. The last drive crosses the cedar forests of the Middle Atlas, with their Barbary macaques, and Ifrane to Fes, where a licensed guide shows you the medieval medina before your departure or an optional extension to Chefchaouen.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: 10 days, 9 nights
• Start: Marrakech (airport or riad) – Finish: Fes (airport, station or riad)
• Type: private tour with your own driver; licensed local guides in Marrakech and Fes, local guide at Ait Ben Haddou
• Total distance: about 1,700 km; most days have 3 to 6 hours on the road, Day 5 is the longest
• Nights: Marrakech (2), Ait Ben Haddou, Ouarzazate, Erg Chebbi desert camp, Dades valley, Midelt, Fes (2)
• Meals: breakfast daily; dinner from Ait Ben Haddou to Midelt (Days 3–7)
• Activity level: easy

WHAT YOU SEE
• Marrakech: the Koutoubia, the Bahia Palace, the Saadian Tombs, the souks, the Majorelle Garden and Jemaa el-Fna.
• The Tizi n'Tichka pass and Ait Ben Haddou at sunset.
• Ouarzazate's Taourirt Kasbah and film studios, and the Fint oasis.
• The Valley of Roses, the Dades valley and the Todra gorge.
• The Erg Chebbi dunes at sunset and sunrise.
• The Ziz gorges and palm groves, Midelt and the Jebel Ayachi.
• The cedar forest of Azrou with its macaques, and Ifrane.
• Fes el-Bali: madrasas, the Qarawiyyin and the Chouara tannery.

WHY THIS ITINERARY WORKS
Most Marrakech-to-Fes tours squeeze the route into three or four long days. This one spreads it over ten, with extra nights where they make the biggest difference: Ait Ben Haddou for the evening light, Ouarzazate for a slow day, and Midelt to break the long northbound drive. You arrive in Fes rested, with a full guided day to enjoy it.

WHO WILL ENJOY IT
First-time visitors, couples, families and older travellers who want to see the great sights without long days on the road, and anyone flying into Marrakech and out of Fes.

WHO MIGHT PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For the version through the Middle Atlas villages, see our [10-day Marrakech to Fes itinerary through the mountains](/en-US/morocco/marrakech/tours/morocco-10-day-itinerary-from-marrakech-to-fes-through-mountains/6853df192b32f46587f2b787). For more freedom on the road, the [Marrakech to Fes private road trip in 10 days](/en-US/morocco/marrakech/tours/marrakech-to-fes-in-10-days-private-morocco-road-trip-via-the-sahara-desert/7c064672216bc9472598c625).

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Pack layers: the Atlas passes and desert nights are cold from November to March, and Midelt and Ifrane can see snow in winter. Bring sun protection, a small bag for the camp night and comfortable shoes for the medinas. Entrance fees, lunches and the city dinners are not included; most sites cost 30 to 120 dirhams.
descriptions:
What to expect: arrival in Marrakech, time to rest at your riad and a first evening in the square of Jemaa el-Fna.

Your driver meets you at Marrakech Menara airport and takes you to your riad; cars cannot enter the medina's lanes, so a porter helps you with your luggage for the last few minutes on foot. After a mint tea on the patio and some rest, walk to Jemaa el-Fna in the late afternoon. At sunset the square fills with smoking food stalls, Gnawa musicians, storytellers and acrobats. Watch it from a café terrace facing the Koutoubia minaret, then eat at the stalls: harira soup, grilled kebabs and fresh orange juice.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
Arrival – Airport pick-up and transfer to your riad.
17:00 – Walk to Jemaa el-Fna.
18:00 – Sunset from a café terrace, then dinner at the stalls.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Keep small change: performers expect a tip if you take a photo.
• At the food stalls, choose busy ones and agree the price before ordering.

INCLUDED: airport transfer, riad with breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: dinner, tips.

Overnight: riad in Marrakech.
Meals: none (breakfast the next morning).

What to expect: a guided day in Marrakech – the Koutoubia, the Bahia Palace, the Saadian Tombs, the souks and the Majorelle Garden.

Your licensed guide meets you after breakfast. Start at the Koutoubia, whose 12th-century minaret is the landmark of the city, then visit the Bahia Palace, built in the late 19th century for a grand vizier, with courtyards of orange trees and painted cedar ceilings, and the Saadian Tombs, walled up for centuries and rediscovered in 1917. Late morning is for the souks – spices, leather, metal lanterns, carpets and the dyers' lane hung with coloured wool. After lunch your driver takes you to the Majorelle Garden, created by the painter Jacques Majorelle and later saved by Yves Saint Laurent, with its cacti, bamboo and electric-blue villa.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
09:00 – Koutoubia and Bahia Palace.
10:30 – Saadian Tombs.
12:00 – The souks.
13:30 – Lunch (not included).
15:00 – Majorelle Garden.
17:00 – Free time.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Majorelle sells timed tickets online and sells out in high season; we book yours when you confirm.

INCLUDED: licensed guide, driver, riad with breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: entrance fees, lunch, tips.

Overnight: riad in Marrakech.
Meals: breakfast.

What to expect: over the High Atlas by the Tizi n'Tichka pass to Ait Ben Haddou, with a guided walk in the ksar and the sunset from its top.

The road leaves Marrakech and climbs through red earth villages and oak and juniper woods to the Tizi n'Tichka, at about 2,260 m the highest main road pass in Morocco. On the south side the landscape turns dry and mineral, with views over terraced Berber villages. You reach Ait Ben Haddou in the early afternoon. This ksar of earthen houses and towers stacked up a hill above the Ounila river has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987 and has appeared in many films. In the late afternoon, when the day visitors have gone, a local guide walks you across the river and up through its lanes to the old granary at the top for the sunset over the valley.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
09:00 – Depart Marrakech.
11:00 – Tizi n'Tichka pass and viewpoints.
14:00 – Arrival in Ait Ben Haddou; lunch (not included).
17:00 – Guided walk in the ksar and sunset from the granary.
19:30 – Dinner at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The pass road has many bends; take motion sickness tablets if you need them.

INCLUDED: driver, local guide in Ait Ben Haddou, hotel with dinner and breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, tips.

Overnight: hotel or kasbah guesthouse in Ait Ben Haddou.
Meals: breakfast, dinner.

What to expect: a slow day around Ouarzazate, the gateway to the desert – the film studios, the Taourirt Kasbah and the hidden palm oasis of Fint.

Ouarzazate is only about half an hour from Ait Ben Haddou, so the day is relaxed. Start at the Atlas film studios, where sets built for desert epics and biblical films still stand among the stones; a guide shows you around the temples and palaces made of plaster and wood. Then visit the Kasbah Taourirt in the town centre, a sprawling earthen residence of the Glaoui family with painted ceilings in its upper rooms. In the afternoon your driver takes you a short way out of town to the Fint oasis, a green ribbon of palms and gardens along a river below black rocks, where a small village keeps a traditional way of life. Walk among the gardens before returning to your hotel.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
09:00 – Atlas film studios (about 1 hour).
11:00 – Kasbah Taourirt (about 1 hour).
13:00 – Lunch (not included).
15:00 – Fint oasis walk (about 1.5 hours).
17:30 – Hotel in Ouarzazate; dinner.

GOOD TO KNOW
• If you prefer, the morning can include the cinema museum or a cooking class instead of the studios.

INCLUDED: driver, hotel with dinner and breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: entrance fees, lunch, tips.

Overnight: hotel in Ouarzazate.
Meals: breakfast, dinner.

What to expect: the longest drive of the trip, east along the Road of a Thousand Kasbahs and through the Todra gorge to Merzouga, and a camel trek to a desert camp at sunset.

You leave early and follow the valley east past Skoura and its palm grove, the Valley of Roses at Kelaat M'Gouna and the entrance to the Dades. At Tinghir you turn into the Todra gorge, where the limestone walls rise about 300 m and close to around ten metres apart; walk along the stream through the narrows. The road then crosses stony plains and oases, past lines of khettara wells, to Erfoud and Merzouga. In the late afternoon leave your luggage in the vehicle, mount your camel and ride for about an hour and a half into the Erg Chebbi as the sand turns orange. Climb a dune for the sunset, then reach your camp for dinner, music around the fire and a sky full of stars.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
07:30 – Depart Ouarzazate.
09:00 – Skoura and the Valley of Roses (short stops).
11:00 – Todra gorge walk (about 1 hour).
12:30 – Lunch (not included).
17:00 – Camel trek into the dunes (about 1.5 hours).
19:00 – Desert camp; dinner.

GOOD TO KNOW
• About 370 km; your driver stops regularly.
• Pack a small bag for the camp: warm layer, torch, toothbrush. Camps with private bathrooms are available on request.

INCLUDED: driver, camel trek, desert camp with dinner and breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, tips.

Overnight: desert camp in the Erg Chebbi.
Meals: breakfast, dinner.

What to expect: sunrise over the Sahara, then back west through the oases to the Dades valley and its red rock formations.

Wake before dawn and climb a dune to watch the sun rise over the sea of sand, then ride the camels back to Merzouga for a shower and breakfast. On the way west you can stop in Rissani, the old capital of the Tafilalet, whose market fills on Sundays, Tuesdays and Thursdays, and see the ksour and palm gardens of the oases. In the afternoon you reach Boumalne and turn up the Dades valley, past the rounded red rocks called the 'monkey fingers', to the hairpin road of Tisdrine and your hotel above the river.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
06:00 – Sunrise from the dunes; camel ride back.
09:00 – Depart Merzouga; Rissani (optional stop).
13:00 – Lunch (not included).
15:00 – Dades valley, the 'monkey fingers' and Tisdrine viewpoint.
17:00 – Hotel in the Dades; dinner.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The Dades valley is cool in the evening; keep a warm layer at hand.

INCLUDED: driver, hotel with dinner and breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, tips.

Overnight: hotel in the Dades valley.
Meals: breakfast, dinner.

What to expect: north through the palm groves of the Ziz and over the eastern High Atlas to Midelt, the apple town below the Jebel Ayachi.

The road runs east past Tinghir and Goulmima to Errachidia, then turns north into the Ziz gorges, where the river has cut a deep, green canyon through the mountains, lined with palms and earthen villages; stop at the viewpoint above the valley. You climb through the tunnel of the Légionnaire and over the Tizi n'Talghemt pass to the high plateaus around Midelt, at about 1,500 m, with the snowy ridge of the Jebel Ayachi (about 3,750 m) on the horizon. Midelt is known for its apples and for its fossil and mineral shops; in the late afternoon you can visit them or walk in the quiet town before dinner.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
09:00 – Depart the Dades.
12:00 – Errachidia; lunch (not included).
14:00 – Ziz gorges and the valley viewpoint.
16:00 – Arrival in Midelt.

GOOD TO KNOW
• This day breaks the long drive to Fes in two, so the next day is short and relaxed.
• In winter the passes can see snow; your driver checks the road.

INCLUDED: driver, hotel with dinner and breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, tips.

Overnight: hotel or guesthouse in Midelt.
Meals: breakfast, dinner.

What to expect: through the cedar forests of the Middle Atlas, where Barbary macaques live wild, and the alpine-style town of Ifrane, to Fes.

The road crosses the high plateau north of Midelt and climbs into the Middle Atlas. Near Azrou you enter the cedar forest, one of the largest in North Africa, where troops of Barbary macaques come down to the roadside; your driver stops so you can watch them from a respectful distance. Ifrane, built in the 1930s with sloping roofs and gardens at 1,650 m, looks more like a mountain town in Europe than in Morocco. In the afternoon you descend through farmland to Fes and settle into your riad in the medina.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
09:00 – Depart Midelt.
11:00 – Cedar forest near Azrou and the macaques.
12:00 – Ifrane; lunch (not included).
15:00 – Arrival at your riad in Fes.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Please do not feed the macaques; it harms them.

INCLUDED: driver, riad with breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, tips.

Overnight: riad in Fes.
Meals: breakfast.

What to expect: a full day in Fes el-Bali, the medieval medina founded in the 9th century, with a licensed guide.

Start at the golden doors of the Royal Palace and in the Mellah, the old Jewish quarter, then enter the medina by Bab Boujloud, the blue gate. Your guide leads you to the Bou Inania madrasa, with its carved cedar, stucco and zellige, and down the Talaa Kebira through the souks. You see the courtyard of the Qarawiyyin from its doors – founded in 859 by Fatima al-Fihri, it is often called the oldest existing university in the world – and visit the Attarine madrasa beside it. After lunch you pass the coppersmiths of the Seffarine square and end on a terrace above the Chouara tannery, where hides are still dyed in stone vats.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
09:00 – Royal Palace gates, the Mellah and Bab Boujloud.
10:00 – Bou Inania madrasa and the souks.
13:00 – Lunch in the medina (not included).
14:00 – Qarawiyyin, Attarine madrasa and the Seffarine square.
15:00 – Chouara tannery terraces.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The Qarawiyyin mosque is closed to non-Muslims.
• Guides take you into workshops; there is never an obligation to buy.

INCLUDED: licensed guide, riad with breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: entrance fees, lunch, tips.

Overnight: riad in Fes.
Meals: breakfast.

What to expect: departure from Fes, or an optional extension to Chefchaouen, the blue town of the Rif.

After breakfast your driver takes you to Fes-Saïs airport or the train station, or you continue your journey. A popular extension is Chefchaouen, about four hours north through olive groves and the Rif foothills, where you can spend a night or two in the blue medina, or continue to Tangier and its ferries to Spain. Tell us when you book and we will add the nights and transfers.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
Morning – Transfer to Fes airport or station, or start the extension.

GOOD TO KNOW
• For an early flight we leave the riad in time; allow at least two hours at the airport.

INCLUDED: final transfer in Fes.
NOT INCLUDED: extension, tips.

Overnight: none (end of the tour).
Meals: breakfast.

faq.question: Where does the tour start and end?
faq.answer: It starts in Marrakech, at the airport or your riad, and ends in Fes on Day 10 with a transfer to the airport or station – or in Chefchaouen if you take the extension.

faq.question: Is the tour private?
faq.answer: Yes. The vehicle, the driver and the guides are only for you and your group, and you can change stops and timings each day.

faq.question: Which meals are included?
faq.answer: Breakfast daily and dinner from Day 3 to Day 7: Ait Ben Haddou, Ouarzazate, the desert camp, the Dades and Midelt. Lunches and the city dinners are not included.

faq.question: How long are the drives?
faq.answer: Most days have three to six hours on the road with stops. Day 5 from Ouarzazate to Merzouga (about 370 km) is the longest; the night in Midelt splits the return north so the last drive to Fes is short.

faq.question: Why so many nights in the south?
faq.answer: To avoid long, tiring days. A night at Ait Ben Haddou gives you the sunset, Ouarzazate gives a slow day, and Midelt breaks the drive north. It is the same route as faster tours, at a comfortable pace.

faq.question: What is the desert camp like?
faq.answer: Berber-style tents in the Erg Chebbi dunes with real beds, blankets, dinner and breakfast. Camps with private bathrooms in each tent are available on request.

faq.question: Do I have to ride a camel?
faq.answer: No. The ride is about an hour and a half each way, but a 4x4 can take you to the camp if you prefer.

faq.question: Are guides included?
faq.answer: Yes: licensed guides for a full day in Marrakech and in Fes, and a local guide at Ait Ben Haddou. Your driver explains the sights along the way.

faq.question: Can we add Chefchaouen?
faq.answer: Yes. The most popular extension is one or two nights in Chefchaouen after Fes, with an optional continuation to Tangier. Tell us when you book.

faq.question: Are entrance fees included?
faq.answer: No. They are paid on the day and are modest: most sites cost 30 to 120 dirhams. We book timed tickets such as the Majorelle Garden for you.

faq.question: Is the tour suitable for children and older travellers?
faq.answer: Yes. The drives are shorter than on most tours and every day has breaks. Children love the camels and macaques; child seats are available on request.

faq.question: When is the best time to go?
faq.answer: Spring (March to May) and autumn (September to November). Winter works with warm clothes – Midelt and Ifrane can be snowy – and July and August are very hot in the south.

faq.question: Can the tour run from Fes to Marrakech instead?
faq.answer: Yes. We can run the same route in reverse, starting in Fes and ending in Marrakech, to fit your flights.
